title: Attention Launchpad: kernel tuner and graceful fallback playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: We observe intermittent latency spikes and throughput regressions during cold-start and short-lived decode bursts when the runtime probes FlashAttention v2/v3 kernels. This ticket implements a lightweight 'Launchpad' tuner that a) collects a warmup fingerprint during the first N requests, b) scores candidate kernels using a stability+latency heuristic, and c) orchestrates a guarded handoff with deterministic fallback rules. Goals: reduce cold-start P95 latency by 15-25% for decoder-heavy workloads, reduce kernel oscillation across short spike windows, and provide an operator-friendly rollback/playbook for incidents.
Acceptance criteria: 1) New tuner reduces median kernel-switch events by >=40% measured on canary cluster; 2) Cold-start P95 latency improvement >=15% for 8k context GPT-style models in perf harness; 3) No increase in OOMs or GPU memory churn in 7-day soak; 4) Rollout has an automated rollback trigger tied to increased 95th latency or error-rate on Canary.
Approach: - Implement Launchpad as a runtime-local component that runs during the first 3 warmup requests (configurable). - Use telemetry histograms already emitted by the kernel prober but add a compact 'stability score' combining variance, OOM-safety margin, and tail latency. - Persist decision for the active connection and a short TTL cache keyed by model+shape to avoid reprobing on replays. - Handoff protocol: 1) probe kernel A on startup with small synthetic micro-batch; 2) if stability_score(A) > threshold, mark active; 3) otherwise select fallback kernel B with conservative memory footprint; 4) for in-flight decodes allow existing KV cache to continue; 5) if subsequent probes suggest regression, trigger safe rollback with a 5s quiesce window.
Tradeoffs considered: - Probing too aggressively reduces latency but increases memory churn; we bias toward conservative handoffs for short-lived requests. - Caching decisions reduces agility for shape shifts; we keep TTL short and invalidate on significant input-size delta.
Test matrix: - Synthetic microbench on CI (shapes: [1,1k,4k,8k], batch sizes: 1..8, precisions: fp16/int8), against FA2 and FA3 variants. - Canary rollout to 10% of runtime fleet with canary traffic dominated by short-lived decodes. - Soak test 72h for memory regressions and 7d production-like traffic for throughput.
Observability: - New telemetry keys: launchpad.probe.latency_ms, launchpad.stability_score, launchpad.decision, launchpad.rollback.reason. - Dashboards: canary-latency (P50/P95/P99), kernel-switch-rate heatmap, GPU memory churn. - Alerting: canary P95 > baseline*1.25 OR kernel-switch-rate > baseline+3sigma -> automatic rollback.
Rollout plan: - Dev PR with unit+integration tests (runtime unit harness) -> internal review. - Merge behind feature flag. - Canary 10% -> monitor 48h -> 50% -> monitor 72h -> 100%. - If canary triggers rollback criteria, automated revert and page ops on-call.
Links: - Design doc (confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/ATTN-LAUNCHPAD-TUNER - Perf harness: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/perf/launchpad-canary - Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12456 - Playbook snippet: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/launchpad-playbook - Related tickets: ENG-42104 (kernel priority queue), ENG-975310 (prefill-circuit-breaker).
Risks and mitigations: - Regression risk: introduce tight safety nets in rollout, add stochastic replay tests. - Observability gaps: add additional histograms and ensure retention for 14 days for canary. - SLO impact: tie rollback to SLO breach thresholds and introduce gradual exposure.
